Chmielnik Old Jewish Cemetery

Jewish Cemetery · Chmielnik, Poland

Demolished. This record shows a tension worth noting: it is categorized as 'fenced and protected,' yet the source's demolished field marks it as 'yes.' Chmielnik's Jewish population reached an extraordinary 5,908 people (87 percent of the town) by 1939, most murdered by the Germans in 1942. This, the older of Chmielnik's two Jewish cemeteries, was ordered closed by authorities as early as 1819-20 due to overcrowding, with its last burial in 1910. A marketplace occupied the site from 1946, and by the 1980s it had been divided among private estates and a kindergarten. In 2014, as part of a synagogue revitalization project, a memorial structure called the 'Shadow House' was opened on the site.
